confirmed.description: The wreck is a different ship in almost every panel, and three different ships appear on page 4 alone. The script and the 2.4 establishing shot call for the chapter 2/3 vessel: black and high-sided, with a carved stern castle and a snapped mainmast, heeled over on a reef offshore.
confirmed.evidence: 2.4: high carved stern castle, masts canted, heeled on the reef (correct). 3.3: a low dark hull with a single upright mast. 3.5: only bare skeletal ribs close inshore, like an old hulk. 4.1: a huge intact ornate galleon stern almost on the beach. 4.4: a small one-masted wreck with rigging. 4.5: a three-masted ship, every mast standing and tattered sails still set, which contradicts the snapped mainmast. 5.1: a small two-masted ship sitting upright far off. Pick the 2.4 ship and redraw or repaint the background wrecks to match.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed, but the problem is narrower than reported. I cropped and zoomed every wreck. Three of the panels are acceptable. The 2.4 ship is heeled, with a carved stern castle and canted masts. 3.3 is consistent with it: a heeled dark hull with canted, broken masts and debris, far off on the rocks (the reviewer's "single upright mast" is not accurate). 5.1 is also consistent: small, far off, heeled, stern castle, canted masts. 4.1 shows a dismasted dark hulk with an ornate carved stern castle. That reads as the same ship from a closer, reversed angle, though it sits much nearer the shore than "offshore on a reef."

The real failure is on page 4, where the wreck changes from panel to panel:
- 4.1: mastless hulk.
- 4.4 (right background): a small, boxy, open-framed hull with one mast, a yard and tattered canvas, and no stern castle.
- 4.5 (right background): a ship with three masts standing and tattered sails still set. This directly contradicts the snapped mainmast in ch3 8.1 and ch4 2.4. It is clearly visible at print size.

3.5 is a lesser drift: its background shows bare skeletal ribs close inshore, which looks like an old rotted hulk rather than the fresh wreck. The script does not ask for a wreck in 4.4 or 4.5, and its revision notes say "The wreck is tied to the chapter 2 and 3 ship." So these are unscripted backgrounds that break a continuity point the script deliberately locked.

Fix: repaint the 4.4 and 4.5 backgrounds, and ideally the 3.5 background, so they show the 2.4 hull (dark, high-sided, carved stern castle, mainmast snapped, heeled on the reef), or remove the wreck from those panels. This is localized background work, not a redraw of the figures, so it is major rather than a blocker.

confirmed.description: A bright white ornamental pattern, like lace or mehndi, shows on the exposed upper side of Nagoji's left forearm. The forearm is meant to lie inner side down, with no mark readable until the 3.2 reveal. It reads as a decorative tattoo, not a burn, and spoils the reveal.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of the foreground forearm (about x 380-520, y 1490-1590 at 1325-wide display scale): a lacy white filigree patch between elbow and wrist on the outer side. Clean it back to sand-crusted skin.

verdict.reason: The pattern is real. In crops of page 2, panel 4, the foreground forearm (about x 530-720, y 2060-2200 at full 1838-wide resolution) has a white, lace-like filigree patch on its exposed upper side between elbow and wrist. At 4x it is clearly a curling ornamental pattern, not sand. The beach sand is tan and grainy; this is white with swirling lines. The script does not allow it: 1.2 and 2.2 say no readable mark until 3.1/3.2, and 2.4 has the forearm lying inner side down. I am downgrading it from major to minor for two reasons. (1) It does not spoil the reveal. The 3.2 brand is a reddish, ridged, raised patch on the inner forearm and looks nothing like this white filigree, so no reader will connect the two. (2) At true print scale (a 1x crop of the 300 DPI file), the patch is about 0.3 in and reads mostly as a pale scuff or salt crust on wet, sand-flecked skin. Only on close inspection does the ornamental, mehndi-like structure come through. It is still a visible stray mark on the most prominent limb in the panel, so it should be cleaned back to plain wet, sand-crusted skin in retouch. That is polish, not a redraw.

confirmed.description: The brand changes design in every panel where it shows. The bible fixes it as one pale, puckered patch of raised ridges, blurred past reading.
confirmed.evidence: 3.2: an angry red-pink puckered rectangular patch above the bandage. 4.1: rows of short dark dashes that look like stitches. 4.3: pink cursive ridges that almost read as script letters ('MiCS'). 5.4: a white scribbled lacy patch. 6.5: four parallel pale curved lines like claw or whip marks. None is a cross, but the reader cannot tell it is the same mark. 4.3 also comes close to legible lettering. Pick the 3.2 form (or a paler version of it) and match the others to it.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, but at minor severity, not major. I zoomed into each panel. The brand is drawn differently in each one: 3.2 is an angry pink, roughly rectangular patch of puckered ridges; 4.3 is pink ridges shaped like cursive letters; 5.4 is a small white lacy blotch; 6.5 is four separate pale curved lines with dot marks, which look like scratches or whip marks rather than a patch. The bible's chapter 4 row calls for one pale, puckered patch of raised ridges. The 6.5 form departs from that most and is the least likely to read as the same mark from 3.2, even though the kapitan is looking at the brand in that panel. Three parts of the original report do not hold up. (1) 4.1: the dotted rows on the forearm are about 0.17 in on the printed page (300 DPI) and look like sand or water drops; they do not read as a design. (2) 4.3: the shapes look like letters only at 5x zoom, are about 0.18 in on the page, cannot be read at that size, and the bible itself describes the brand as 'old burned letters blurred past reading'. That is not near-legible lettering. (3) 3.2: the angry colour is what the script asks for ('puckered and angry'), so the pink-to-pale change is partly sanctioned. Every instance except the 3.2 insert is about 1/8 to 1/5 inch on the page, so the mismatch is only visible on close reading. Fix: redraw the brand on 6.5, and optionally 5.4, as a paler version of the 3.2 patch. No redraw of 4.1 or 4.3 is needed.

confirmed.description: Wrong speaker tail. The Fisherman's line "Come, bhau. Before the crabs claim you." has a tail that ends in Nagoji's hair, right beside his face, so it reads as Nagoji speaking. The balloon also sits across Nagoji's chin, neck and carried torso, so it hides the shoulders-and-legs carry that the panel exists to show.
confirmed.evidence: page-04.png, about x 480-1020, y 2100-2230 (original px). The tail tip is at about x 540, y 2030, inside Nagoji's curls; the Fisherman's grinning face is above and left, at about x 500-600, y 1950-2010. The "You see..." tail correctly reaches the Fisherman's chest, so the panel has two tails that seem to come from two different men.

verdict.reason:
The tail problem is real, but it is minor, not major. On page 4, panel 4.5 (page-04.png in render r11), the tip of the "Come, bhau. Before the crabs claim you." tail ends at about x 556, y 2035 in original pixels. That point is inside Nagoji's hair, and the right edge of the tail runs along his cheek from y 2035 to 2100. That is a lettering flaw, and it shows even when the image is shrunk to print size.

It does not read as Nagoji speaking, for four reasons:
- The tail points almost straight up (base about 575,2100 to tip 556,2035). Followed upward, that line hits the Fisherman's open, grinning mouth at about 545,1993. The tip stops only about 20 px below his beard.
- Nagoji's mouth is closed and his eyes are half shut. His mouth sits to the right of the tip and below it, not where the tail points.
- The words name the speaker. The Fisherman alone calls Nagoji "bhau" (page 1), and "before the crabs claim you" is said to the man being carried.
- The "You see..." tail ends about 60 px away on the Fisherman's chest, so both tails meet under his chin. They do not split between two men.

The second claim is mostly wrong. The balloon top sits just below Nagoji's chin, which stays visible. The balloon hides his neck and shoulders and the Fisherman's grip there. The carry still reads clearly: the Fisherman's head and body behind Nagoji's head, Nagoji's limp body and bandaged hand hanging, and the Young Fisherman holding his legs in full view.

Fix for polish: extend or re-angle the tail about 25 to 40 px up and to the left so it ends in the Fisherman's beard, not in Nagoji's curls.

confirmed.description: Wrong speaker tail. The girl whispering "<Portuguese.>" is the far-left child with her hand cupped to her mouth, but the tail ends on the back of the head of the child next to her, who is listening.
confirmed.evidence: page-05.png, balloon at about x 555-820, y 985-1105. The tail tip is at about x 465, y 1070, on the back-turned child's hair. The whispering girl's face and cupped hand are at about x 290-410, y 1000-1130. A dashed whisper balloon would also suit the beat better.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page-05.png, panel 5.2. Script 5.2 gives the line to "a small girl" who "whispers to the child beside her." In the art, the girl on the far left (about x 290-410, y 1000-1130) is the one whispering: her hand is cupped at her mouth and turned toward the next child's ear. The second child is turned away toward the carry party and is only listening, so neither her mouth nor her face is shown. The tail of the "<Portuguese.>" balloon (balloon at about x 555-820, y 985-1105) comes to a point at about x 460, y 1070, right on the back of the second child's hair. It stops roughly 65-100 px (a quarter inch at print size) short of the whisperer's hand. A reader following the tail will read the listener as the speaker. The whisper gesture blunts this a little, and the beat (village children naming him Portuguese) survives either way. Still, it is a tail pointing at the wrong character, which the rubric calls major. It is not a blocker because the cast, the beat and the lettering are all correct. The fix is local: re-aim or extend the tail to end at the left girl's cupped hand or mouth. Switching to a dashed whisper balloon would be optional polish, not part of the defect.

refuted.description: Ibrahim (kapitan) reads as the tallest man in the room, which breaks the bible's base line for him: 'shorter than the fishermen but broader'. The script fixes the scale cue as 'the Young Fisherman stands just behind him, half a head taller'. Ibrahim's face itself matches the sheet: white turban, grey-flecked black beard, cream pocketed vest over a white mundu, no coat, and a thin red scar running from his LEFT ear to his jaw.
refuted.reason:
The claim is refuted. In panel 6.5 Ibrahim is the nearest standing figure, and the camera sits low, as the script asks: "Camera low, from beside Nagoji's mat, looking up". With a low camera, the nearest man's head will always rise highest in the frame, so his turban touching the top border shows depth, not height. The art bears this out. Both fishermen's feet sit on the bottom border, but Ibrahim's mundu runs past it and his feet are off-panel, so he is clearly in front.

I measured the panel at 300 DPI. The sea line in the doorway (about y=705 in a crop of the panel's right half) works as the camera horizon, and it crosses both fishermen just above their ankles. Ibrahim's face is about 1.4 to 1.5 times the size of the Young Fisherman's (eye-to-mouth 37 px vs 25 px). Using that scale and the same horizon, Ibrahim's feet would fall about 35 px below the panel edge, which matches the crop. Scaled back to the fishermen's depth, he comes out at roughly 75 to 80 percent of the Young Fisherman's height, so he is shorter, not taller.

The "no broader" part is also wrong. His shoulder span is about 384 px, or roughly 265 px at the fishermen's depth, against about 220 px for the Fisherman (red lungi). His vest-and-mundu silhouette is the widest in the panel.

The literal "half a head taller" side-by-side cue is not drawn, but the scale is legible through perspective. Readers take a foreground figure as larger because he is nearer. At print size this is not a problem worth redrawing.

refuted.description: The Woman (healer) changes from panel to panel. The script describes her as heavy-set and in her fifties, with a low grey-streaked knot, coarse undyed cotton and no fitted blouse. By 6.1 she is slim and younger, and wears what reads as a short-sleeved blouse under her drape.
refuted.reason: I zoomed in on the Woman in 5.4, 5.5 and 6.1, and the art does not support a major costume or identity break. (1) The "sleeve" in 6.1 is the end of her drape over the right shoulder. You can see skin through the cloth, and there is no blouse hem or fitted bodice anywhere. 5.4 draws the drape the same way: the cloth over both shoulders falls to the upper arm like cap sleeves. That matches the script's "end drawn over both shoulders". The V at her chest comes from the drape crossing, as it does in 5.4. A darker stripe at the edge of the cloth is not forbidden, and in that firelight it reads as shadow. (2) 5.5 is consistent. She has the same grey-streaked hair, now visibly in a low knot (closer to the script than 5.4), the same coarse undyed drape and a broad, heavy body under the cloth. Her face looks sharper because the script asks for "her mouth pulled tight". (3) In 6.1 her face is a little narrower and her hair a little darker than in 5.4, but she still reads as about fifty, with heavy grey streaks and lined brows, and her build is average rather than slim. At print size she is under an inch tall. The same drape, clay basin and wrung cloth carry straight on from 5.5, so a reader sees the same woman. Some slight face drift between generated panels remains, but it is too small to matter in print, so the claim is refuted.

refuted.description: Anachronistic tailoring on the kapitan. He wears a tailored waistcoat with four buttons and two flap patch pockets over a long-sleeved, band-collared shirt with the cuffs rolled. That reads as a 19th or 20th-century waistcoat-over-kurta outfit, not 1753 Malabar dress. The script calls for only a 'pale vest over a white mundu'. Redraw it as a plain, unbuttoned cloth upper garment with no pockets and no fitted shirt underneath.
refuted.reason: The art matches the description: at page 6, panel 5 the kapitan wears a cream vest with buttons and flap patch pockets over a band-collared long-sleeved shirt with rolled cuffs, and a white mundu and striped shoulder cloth. But this is his approved design, not a drift. The approved sheet concepts/09-ibrahim-marakkar-v15.png (registered in APPROVED-SHEETS.json) shows this exact garment: the same buttoned cream vest with flap pockets, the same collared shirt with rolled sleeves, the mundu and the blue-striped shoulder cloth. Its details row even labels the pockets "BULGING VEST POCKETS". The bible also gives him a vest with bulging pockets (CONTINUITY.md, Ibrahim row 6-28). The chapter 4-5 row ("Pale vest over a white mundu, no coat") is that same sheet outfit with the teal coat taken off, and the render follows it: the vest is pale and there is no coat. The script's "pale vest over a white mundu" does not ban buttons or pockets, and it does not ask for a "plain unbuttoned cloth upper garment". The suggested redraw would break continuity with the approved sheet and with chapter 6 onward. Any period-accuracy objection belongs against the approved character design, not this panel.

refuted.description: The brand on Nagoji's left forearm is painted as a looping cursive scrawl that reads like handwritten letters (roughly 'mcgu'). The 3.2 insert shows lumpy raised ridges instead. The script requires 'crude marks blurred past reading. No legible letters'. As drawn it reads as script on his skin, and it does not match the brand in 3.2.
refuted.reason: I cropped page-04.png at x 560-920, y 1640-1940 and the brand itself at x 700-830, y 1760-1880, looked at it at native and pixel-level zoom, and compared it with the page 3, panel 2 insert. The art does not support a major. (1) The marks are pale, raised scar ridges on the inner side of the left forearm, just above the wrist bandage. They sit in a short row and suggest letter shapes, but no letter or word can be read. Even at 6x pixel zoom the strokes could be taken for "ANGU", "mcgu" or "ANSUG", and that ambiguity is what "blurred past reading" means. The bible's chapter 4 row allows exactly this: "a pale puckered patch of raised ridges, the shape of old burned letters blurred past reading, no legible letters, no numerals, and not a cross." There are no numerals and no cross. (2) At print size (the page is 1838 px across a 6.125 in bleed width, so about 300 ppi), the brand is about 75 x 70 px, roughly 0.25 in or 6 mm. A reader sees a small pale scribbled scar, not writing. (3) It does not match page 3, panel 2 exactly. There the brand is a reddish puckered rectangular plaque with ridges inside; here it is paler loose ridges with no plaque edge. But it is in the same place, on the same arm, and both read as raised ridged burn scars, so the difference is not noticeable at this panel's scale. A colourist could tint it toward the reddish 3.2 look, but that is optional polish, not a costume or continuity error that needs a redraw.

refuted.description: Wrong speaker tail: the balloon "Come, bhau. Before the crabs claim you." points at Nagoji's head, not at the Fisherman's mouth, so the line reads as Nagoji's. The script gives both 4.5 balloons to the Fisherman.
refuted.reason: I'm treating this as refuted: the art doesn't make the line read as Nagoji's. I traced the tail pixel by pixel. Its tip is at about (556, 2043) on the 1838x2775 page. The tail rises almost straight up and leans slightly left. Its centre moves from about x=562 at y=2105 to x=556 at the tip. Extend that line about 50 px (about 4 mm at 300 DPI) and it reaches the grinning Fisherman's mouth and grey beard, at about (550, 1990). The tip does touch the top-left edge of Nagoji's hair. But that is just where Nagoji's head rests against the Fisherman's chest, directly below the Fisherman's chin. Nagoji's own face and mouth sit further right and lower, about 65 px from the tip, while the Fisherman's mouth is about 50 px away. So the tip is closer to the Fisherman's mouth, and the tail's direction points at him, not at Nagoji's face. The words also settle who is speaking. "Come, bhau. Before the crabs claim you." is said to the man being carried, so Nagoji cannot be the speaker. It also follows the Fisherman's first balloon in the same panel, which matches the script, since both 4.5 lines belong to the Fisherman. At print size this is not a wrong speaker tail. The only possible polish is lengthening the tail about 40 to 50 px so it ends on the beard instead of touching Nagoji's hair, and that is too slight to flag.

refuted.description: The kapitan's costume does not match the script or the bible row for chapters 4 and 5 ("pale vest over a white mundu, no coat"). He wears a long-sleeved, band-collared shirt with rolled cuffs under a buttoned waistcoat with flap patch pockets, plus a blue-striped towel. It reads as a 20th-century shirt-and-waistcoat outfit, and it anticipates the chapter 6 coat with bulging pockets.
refuted.reason:
I zoomed into the kapitan in page 6, panel 5. The reviewer describes the art correctly: a cream five-button vest with two flap pockets, a band-collared white shirt with rolled sleeves under it, a blue-striped shoulder towel and a white mundu. But the costume is allowed, so this is not a defect.

1. The approved character sheet (concepts/09-ibrahim-marakkar-v15.png, listed as "ibrahim" in APPROVED-SHEETS.json) shows the same pieces under his teal short coat: the cream button vest with flap pockets, a band-collared white shirt at the neck, the white mundu and the blue-striped fringed towel. The panel is that approved look with only the coat left off, which is what the bible's chapter 4-5 row asks for ("Pale vest over a white mundu, no coat").

2. The pockets do not jump ahead to chapter 6. The bible's chapter 6-28 row reads "Short coat over a vest with bulging pockets", and the sheet's detail box is labelled "BULGING VEST POCKETS". The pockets belong to the vest he already wears in chapters 4-5. Only the coat arrives in chapter 6, and he has no coat here.

3. The bible and the script both describe the vest and the mundu, and neither rules out an under-shirt. The shirt matches the approved sheet. The "20th-century" reading is a judgment about the sheet's design, not a mismatch in this panel. If the author wants that changed, it is a change to the approved sheet, not a redraw of this page.

refuted.description: The script's scale beat is reversed. The script and the bible base line say the kapitan is "shorter than the fishermen but broader", with the Young Fisherman "half a head taller" just behind him. In the art the kapitan is the tallest figure in the frame and towers over both fishermen. This is his first appearance and sets his build for later chapters.
refuted.reason:
Refuted. The reviewer's evidence compares head tops on the page and ignores depth. The script asks for a low camera looking up, and the kapitan stands several paces closer to it than the fishermen do. His face is drawn about 1.5 times the Young Fisherman's: eye to chin is about 63 px against 42 px at full resolution. So in this shot his head would sit higher on the page even if he were shorter.

The horizon check points the same way. The sea horizon through the doorway is at about y=2445 at full resolution, and the fishermen's feet are at about y=2537. The ratio of head-above-horizon to horizon-above-feet works out to about 6.8 for the Young Fisherman and about 6.0 for the Fisherman. For the kapitan it is about 5.7 to 6.6 at skull height, and his feet are below the panel edge. By that measure he is no taller than the Young Fisherman and probably shorter.

He also reads as built the way the bible says. In head units he is a stocky figure of about 6 heads, with a heavy torso under the vest. Both fishermen are lean and long-limbed. Nothing in the panel sets him up as tall for later chapters.

One small polish point remains. The script puts the Young Fisherman "just behind him, half a head taller", but here the fishermen stand a few paces back. Because of that, the panel never shows the "shorter than the fishermen" comparison directly. That is minor at most, not a reversed beat.

refuted.description: Wrong speaker tail on the girl's whisper. The "<Portuguese.>" tail points at the back of the head of the listening child. The whispering girl, the one with her hand cupped to her mouth whom the script makes the speaker, is not the tail's target.
refuted.reason: I zoomed in on page 5, panel 2 (original pixels about x 330 to 620, y 980 to 1130). The tail tip does stop on the listening child's hair, at about (459, 1071) in original pixels. But the tail is aimed at the whispering girl. Its nearly horizontal lower edge, extended left, runs straight to her nose and upper lip, where her mouth is hidden behind her cupped hand at about (400, 1085). The listener's head simply sits between the balloon and the whisperer's mouth. When a speaker's mouth is blocked like this, aiming the tail through the blocking figure is a normal lettering choice. The tail cannot touch the whisperer's mouth anyway, because her hand covers it. The tip lands about 60 px past her mouth, which is roughly 5 mm on the printed page. The cupped hand is the strongest cue in the panel, so a reader will take her as the speaker. The listener has her back to us and shows no mouth. The script's beat is also intact: a village child says "Portuguese." Panel 5.3 then follows with the Young Fisherman turning on "the girl," and nothing there depends on which of the two children spoke. This does not misattribute the line in any way that matters at print size. At most, a letterer could pull the tip back about 60 px as optional polish. It is not a major error.

minors.description: The Fisherman (the leader) is drawn as a different face in the panel meant to establish all three men at full figure for the chapter. 2.1 set him up as a lean face with a full short grizzled grey beard, grey-streaked hair and a grin. In 2.4 he is heavy-jowled and scowling, with black hair and a thick black upturned moustache, and the grey shows only as stubble on his chin. The top of his head is also cut off at the forehead by the panel border.
minors.evidence: Upper middle of 2.4, the red-lungi figure with the white cloth: his face is cropped by the top border, and zoomed in it shows a black handlebar moustache over grey chin stubble. Compare 2.1 (left face, grey full beard) and 2.2 (grizzled grey beard).

minors.description: The Fisherman drifts again into the black-moustache version from 2.4: black curly hair, a thick black curled moustache and grey only as chin stubble. In 5.2 he is shoulder to shoulder with Nagoji, and both read as curly-black-haired men with thick curled black moustaches. That is a look-alike risk for the hero at small size. He goes back to a grey beard and grey-streaked hair in 5.3 to 5.5.
minors.evidence: 5.1, left carrier in the red lungi: black hair, black handlebar moustache, little grey. 5.2, the man behind Nagoji's left shoulder (white cloth): same black moustache and black hair, directly beside Nagoji's matching moustache. Compare 5.3 (right, grey beard) and 3.4 or 3.5 (grey hair, grey beard).

minors.description: The Fisherman (red lungi) looks like a younger, different man in 6.5: black curly hair, a full dark beard greying only at the chin, and a gaunter face. In 6.3 on the same page he has grey-streaked hair and a grizzled grey beard. His white shoulder cloth has also picked up blue stripes and a fringe that copy Ibrahim's shawl, where the script calls for a plain white cotton cloth. In 6.4 he wears a gold earring, which is Nagoji's signature accessory.
minors.evidence: 6.5, far right figure in the red lungi: dark hair and dark beard, and the cloth on his left shoulder has blue stripe bands like the shawl on Ibrahim beside him. 6.3: same man with grey-streaked hair and a grey beard. 6.4, blurred background: a gold drop earring on the Fisherman's ear.

minors.description: The Young Fisherman wears a small gold ear stud. That is Nagoji's identifying accessory, and on a man who also has curly black hair and a moustache it blurs the hero's signature. The stud is not part of the Young Fisherman's spec and is not visible in 2.1, 2.4, 4.1 or 5.3.
minors.evidence: 4.5, the man in the headband carrying the legs: zoomed in, a gold stud shows on his ear below the headband knot.

minors.description: Nagoji's brand, which the bible makes part of his chapter 4 identity, is drawn differently from panel to panel, and in 4.3 it is on the wrong side of the arm. Here it is a row of separate ridged glyphs that almost read as letters, on the outer (back) side of the left forearm, because the bandaged hand rests palm-down on his knee. 3.2 set it up as one amorphous puckered patch on the inner forearm. 5.4 shows a pale smear, and 6.5 shows parallel stitch-like ridges. The bible requires one mark on the inner side, blurred past reading.
minors.evidence: 4.3, viewer's right: the left forearm lies across his knee with the knuckles up, and the mark sits on its upper face as about five letter-like ridged shapes. Compare the 3.2 insert (a single raised blob), 5.4 (a pale patch above the wrist bandage) and 6.5 (rows of short parallel ridges).

minors.description: The Fisherman's white shoulder cloth flips to his RIGHT shoulder. The script sets it on his LEFT shoulder (2.1, 2.4, 6.3), and 2.2, 2.4, 3.1, 3.4, 4.1, 5.4, 6.1 and 6.3 keep it there.
minors.evidence: 3.5: he faces right toward Nagoji, and the cloth covers his near (right) shoulder at the left frame edge. 5.5: he faces right, and the cloth drapes his near (right) shoulder. 4.5: the visible cloth hangs from his right side while he carries Nagoji's shoulders.

minors.description: The Fisherman's plain white shoulder cloth has turned into a fringed cloth with light-blue stripes, the same design as the kapitan's cloth on the Ibrahim sheet. The two men's props now merge in the one panel where they stand together.
minors.evidence: 6.5, right-hand figure in the red lungi: a cream cloth with pale-blue stripe borders and a fringe, matching Ibrahim's cloth in the same frame. In every earlier panel his cloth is plain white with no stripes.

minors.description: The Young Fisherman wears a small gold ear stud. That is Nagoji's identifying mark, and nobody else's costume includes it.
minors.evidence: Zoom on the Young Fisherman's head (headband figure, centre): a gold stud in his visible ear. No other panel gives him one.

minors.description: Nagoji's chest rope burns have become a single straight healed scar like a surgical line. In 3.1, 5.4 and 5.5 they are several raw red chafe bands.
minors.evidence: 6.4: one thin, clean horizontal line across both pectorals. 5.4 and 5.5: multiple red, raw criss-cross burns.

minors.description: The kapitan reads as taller than the fishermen. The bible and script make him shorter but broader, with the Young Fisherman just behind him and half a head taller. Here the fishermen stand several paces back and look smaller.
minors.evidence: Ibrahim fills the frame top to bottom. The Young Fisherman and the Fisherman stand well behind, their heads level with his shoulders, so the height relationship the script asks for is not shown.

minors.description: The rope rig changes between 1.2 and 1.3. In 1.3 the rope runs over the top of his shoulder close to the neck. The script asks for two loops across the chest under the armpits, well clear of the neck. 1.2 shows only one loop under the arms.
minors.evidence: 1.3: a rope strand rises over the shoulder beside the neck, with more turns around the upper arm. 1.2: a single loop under the arms, with the free end trailing into the surf.

minors.description: The raw chafe rings at the ankles where the irons bit (script 1.2) are not drawn, even where his bare ankles are prominent.
minors.evidence: 4.5 and 5.2: Nagoji's bare ankles and feet are in clear view with clean, unmarked skin.

minors.description: Some villagers wear stitched sleeved tops. The script asks for plain mundu with an upper cloth over both shoulders, and no fitted blouses.
minors.evidence: The foreground girl wears a maroon short-sleeved fitted top. The woman in the left doorway and the far-left woman behind the fence wear white tops with sleeves.

minors.description: The background village houses have regular coursed clay-tile roofs that look like Mangalore tiles. The script specifies palm-thatch roofs. Tiled roofs on commoners' houses are anachronistic for a 1738-1753 Kerala fishing village: tiles were a restricted privilege, and the Mangalore pattern dates from 1865. Panel 5.3 correctly shows thatch.
minors.evidence: page-05.png, panel 5.2, right half of the background behind the Young Fisherman, roughly x 1100-1450, y 870-1000 in original pixels: tiled roof planes over the laterite house.

minors.description: Fitted, sleeved blouses appear in the village. The foreground girl wears a red short-sleeved fitted blouse. A background woman at right-centre appears to wear a sleeved white top, and in 5.3 the girl in the doorway wears a sleeved top with a long skirt. The script requires 'no fitted blouses', and the sleeved blouse is a 19th to 20th-century garment in Kerala.
minors.evidence: page-05.png, panel 5.2: girl at far left, about x 240-330, y 1080-1195 (red sleeve on her upper arm). Background woman at about x 1250-1320, y 990-1110. Panel 5.3: girl in the doorway at about x 300-340, y 1360-1470.

minors.description: The carved panels on the wreck's stern castle form glyph-like shapes that resemble letters or numerals (roughly '3S'). They are near-illegible at print size but count as pseudo-text in the art. Soften them to plain ornament.
minors.evidence: page-02.png, panel 2.4, wreck stern at roughly x 1530-1650, y 1790-1850 in original pixels, the row of carved panels below the stern gallery rail.

minors.description: Ragged page frame. Four of the five panels (5.1, 5.2, 5.4, 5.5) are inset about 83 px on each side, and only 5.3 runs the full live width. The page reads as a narrow column with one panel sticking out on both sides. No Chapter 1 page has most of its tiers inset like this.
minors.evidence: Measured outer borders: 5.1, 5.2, 5.4 and 5.5 run x 231-1606; 5.3 runs x 148-1688 (y 1206-1562). Chapter 1 p.1 has every tier at x 148-1688.

minors.description: The two-up top row is misaligned. 6.2 starts 16 px lower and ends 12 px higher than 6.1, so the top and bottom borders step across the gutter.
minors.evidence: 6.1 spans y 358-914 and 6.2 spans y 374-902 (original px). The step is visible at the top and bottom of the gutter at x about 915-925.

minors.description: The script asks for a "Full-width tier, not a narrow strip", but 6.4 is inset about 38 px on each side. Its edges do not line up with 6.3 above or 6.5 below, which both run the full width.
The script calls for "Wide, full width" in 4.1 and "Full width" in 4.5, but both are inset about 39 px a side. The two middle tiers are the full width, so the page frame steps in, out, out, in.

"You see, he has a tongue as well as scars." is squeezed into a tall, narrow balloon pressed against the left border, with one to three words per line (You see, / he has a / tongue as / well as / scars.). It reads choppy and is out of line with the wide balloons everywhere else.
minors.evidence: page-04.png, about x 190-410, y 1955-2240. The balloon's left edge touches the panel border at x 187.

minors.description: The stacked captions are misaligned and the first one merges with the panel frame. "His eyes moved over me..." sits right on the left border with no inset and shares its border line. The second caption below it is inset about 12 px and is narrower, so the stack looks ragged on the chapter's final, largest panel.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, caption 1 at x 148-750, y 1765-1895, drawn over the 148 px border; caption 2 at about x 165-730, y 1905-2040.

minors.description: The last caption, "In that silence, I was being weighed.", sits on Nagoji's chest and shoulder. That is exactly the area the kapitan's appraising look moves over (brand, hands, shoulders). The empty floor at lower right, below and between the standing men, would keep Nagoji's body clear.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, caption at about x 285-745, y 2290-2385, directly below Nagoji's face (about x 530-610, y 2110-2200) and over his torso.

minors.description: Two very large balloons fill about half of a small panel. The speaker, the Fisherman, is a small figure squeezed between them, with one balloon tail from above and one from below. The top balloon is set in three short lines and jammed into the top-right corner against both borders.
minors.evidence: page-06.png: top balloon at about x 580-915, y 360-590, touching the top border (y 358) and right border (x 915); bottom balloon at about x 320-705, y 670-905. The Fisherman's head is at about x 490-560, y 570-650, between them.

minors.description: Three Fisherman balloons zig-zag: top centre, then far right, then back to lower left. A reader scanning left to right can easily read "<We might as well gain something.>" (lower left) before "<You think leaving one marata...>" (right), and that reverses the argument's build.
minors.evidence: page-03.png: balloon 2 at about x 965-1590, y 1910-2085; balloon 3 at about x 450-955, y 2035-2160. Both have tails to the same speaker, and balloon 3 sits left of and only slightly below balloon 2.

minors.description: The tail of the off-panel voice "See the brand on his arm." runs the full height of the panel, about 330 px, from the bottom-right corner up to the top border, and cuts between the walkers' legs. The other two voices have short tails into the legs. The balloon also sits flush against the bottom and right borders.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, balloon at about x 1315-1685, y 2420-2530. The tail rises from about y 2420 to the top border at about y 2068 near x 1520.

minors.description: In this short strip the three heads are jammed against the top border (the Young Fisherman's headband and Nagoji's hair are clipped). The "<He has soldier's calluses...>" balloon overlaps the Young Fisherman's ear and jaw, with its tail sitting on his beard.
minors.evidence: page-03.png, panel spans y 358-686. The balloon's right edge, at about x 590-620, y 380-470, overlaps the Young Fisherman's face at about x 600-700.

minors.description: The bottom strip crops Nagoji's forehead and the Fisherman's head at the top border. The balloons then fill the middle band, so the two faces are wedged into the top 60 px of the panel.
minors.evidence: page-05.png, panel spans y 2154-2542. Nagoji's face is at about x 760-840, y 2160-2230, with the top of his head cut off by the border.

minors.description: Lettering style has drifted from the approved Chapter 1. Chapter 4 captions are centred, while Chapter 1 captions are left-aligned (for example p.1 "I was Nagoji Sawant..."). This holds on every Chapter 4 page, so the two chapters will look letter-set differently side by side.
minors.evidence: Compare ch04 r11 page-01, caption 1.1 "When the sea finally spat me out..." (centred, with "ceremony." alone on a centred second line), with ch01 r6 page-01, where captions are left-aligned. The same centring appears in the 2.2, 2.3, 4.3, 5.1, 6.2 and 6.4 captions.

minors.description: The script asks for a ground-level tight shot of the hands dug into the grit while he is still collapsed. The art is a medium shot of Nagoji up on hands and knees, pushing off the sand, with his moustache and ear stud in frame. Panel 1.3 then shows him flat again with his cheek on the sand, so the sequence reads as crawl up, then fall back.
minors.evidence: In the second panel, his torso is raised on straight arms and his knees are under him in the surf. His lower face is visible at the top edge, at about (430-760, 565-670) on the displayed page.

minors.description: The light shift goes too far. 1.4 is a golden sunset with sunbeams breaking through. 2.1, the next moment, is under a flat, lowering grey overcast sky as scripted. The jump reads as a different time of day rather than the same grey storm-spent afternoon.
minors.evidence: The bottom strip shows a bright sun and rays at upper left (about 360, 1530 on the displayed page) and gold reflections on the wet sand. The full page-2 tier 2.1 shows uniform grey cloud.

minors.description: The wreck does not hold as the chapter 2 and 3 ship the script names in 2.4 (black, high-sided, carved stern castle, mainmast snapped). In 3.3 it is a low, small hull with thin masts. In 4.5 it has masts standing with sails hanging, even though the mainmast was snapped in 2.4.
minors.evidence: Compare the far-right ship in 2.4 (carved stern castle, at about 1300-1470 x, 1240-1340 y), the mid-background hull in 3.3 (about 650-830 x, 915-1000 y), and the ship in 4.5 (about 1010-1180 x, 1490-1660 y, with masts and sails standing).

minors.description: The caption "After the dungeon and the storm, these small things felt like gifts." covers the Wary Fisherman, who the script says leads the carry party. Only his head and shoulders show, so the leader reads as a cropped bystander.
minors.evidence: The caption box at about (640-1040, 515-605) on the displayed page covers his torso and legs below the net. Only his head is visible, at about (790, 460).

minors.description: Staging is off. The script puts the boy in the doorway, backlit by grey daylight, panting, with one hand on the frame. In the art he is outside in the rain, front-lit, running toward the door, with no hand on the frame.
minors.evidence: In the top-right panel, the boy stands at about (705, 470) on the displayed page, past the door frame, on a wet path outside. Rain and palms are behind him, and his face and front are lit.

minors.description: The arrival beat is weakened. The script has the Fisherman and the Young Fisherman both turning their heads toward the door and straightening as the shadow falls. Only the Young Fisherman looks toward the door. The Fisherman looks back toward Nagoji and the camera.
minors.evidence: The background figures sit at about (630, 1030) for the Fisherman, who faces the camera, and (740, 1040) for the Young Fisherman, who looks right. The doorway and shadow are at far right (about 1000-1180 x, 1080-1250 y).
